advances:
This replaces the single spanning-face estimate by the exact visible-fan
formula for an arbitrary polygonal singleton frontier.  For any deepest
added point \(P\), every visible edge contributes one disjoint triangle,
and clipping that triangle by the two adjacent walls gives a sharp
lower bound for the two transverse added caps.  The formula has no
slope denominators, so wall-parallel faces, wall vertices, and zero
support reaches are included.  An exact two-edge example shows that no
subface or adjacent pair must dominate a fictitious spanning chord:
an internal singleton face can be the only visible face and then all
added area is singleton area while both transverse charges are zero.
The remaining endpoint task is to bound the capacity of this
zero-charge visibility region, or to prove that the required crossing
mass leaves it.

proof:
The affine coordinate map in (2) is nonsingular because
\(\nabla f_2,\nabla f_3\) are not parallel.  Its Jacobian gives (3).
Since \(f_1=-1-S-T\), the open first quadrant is exactly the
singleton-\(1\) chamber, proving (4).

For a counterclockwise edge \(D_j\), the polygon lies in the closed
left halfplane
\[
\det(D_j,X-V_j)\geq0.
\]
This is equivalent to \(\lambda_j(X)\leq0\) on \(B\).  If
\(\lambda_j(P)>0\), every point of
\(\operatorname{conv}\{P,V_j,V_{j+1}\}\) having positive barycentric
weight at \(P\) has positive \(\lambda_j\), and therefore lies outside
\(B\).  The coordinate area of this triangle is
\[
\frac{\lambda_j(P)}2.
\tag{28}
\]

The two supporting rays from an exterior point \(P\) to a convex
polygon determine one visible boundary arc.  Hence the positive
\(\lambda_j(P)\) form one cyclic interval.  The triangles in (28) over
that interval have disjoint interiors and their union, up to boundary,
is
\[
\operatorname{conv}(B\cup\{P\})\setminus B.
\tag{29}
\]
This follows directly by replacing the visible boundary arc of \(B\)
with the two tangent segments from its endpoints to \(P\); the fan from
\(P\) triangulates the polygon between the old and new arcs.

It remains to compute the fraction of one fan triangle in a wall
halfplane.  If exactly one vertex value of an affine function is
negative, the negative part is the similar corner triangle obtained
by cutting the two incident sides.  Its two linear scale factors are
\[
\frac{-a_{(1)}}{a_{(2)}-a_{(1)}},
\qquad
\frac{-a_{(1)}}{a_{(3)}-a_{(1)}}.
\]
Their product gives the third case in (6).  If exactly two values are
negative, the positive complement is the similar corner triangle at
the positive vertex, with area fraction
\[
\frac{a_{(3)}^2}
{(a_{(3)}-a_{(1)})(a_{(3)}-a_{(2)})}.
\]
This gives the fourth case.  The all-positive and all-negative cases
give the first two cases, and the formulas are continuous when a
single value is zero.  This proves the clipping interpretation of
\(\vartheta\).

Apply that interpretation to the affine coordinate \(S\) on every
triangle in (29), add the disjoint triangle contributions, and multiply
by \(\gamma\).  Since
\(\operatorname{conv}(B\cup\{P\})\subseteq K\), this proves (8).
The same argument with \(T\) proves (9).  When (10) holds, (29) is the
whole added region, so both inequalities are equalities.

For (11), the clockwise normal
\[
(D_{j,T},-D_{j,S})
\]
has length \(|D_j|\) and points to the exterior side.  It is therefore
\[
\frac{|D_j|}{\sqrt{a_j^2+b_j^2}}(a_j,b_j).
\]
Taking its scalar product with \(P-V_j\) proves (11).

The function in (12) is continuous.  It vanishes on \(B\), so a
maximizer exists on the compact set
\(K\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}\).  If \(K\) has the form (10), every
point is a convex combination of \(P\) and a point of \(B\).  Affinity
of each \(\lambda_j\) then gives
\[
\delta_B(X)\leq\delta_B(P),
\]
proving the deepest-point assertion.

Suppose \(P\) lies in the open quadrant.  If
\(P\in\mathcal Z_B\), every visible edge has both endpoints in the
closed quadrant.  Its fan triangle is consequently contained in that
quadrant, so both clipping fractions in (8)--(9) vanish.  Conversely,
if \(P\notin\mathcal Z_B\), some charging edge is visible.  At least
one of its endpoint coordinates is strictly negative, whereas the
corresponding coordinate of \(P\) is positive.  Formula (6) then gives
a strictly positive clipping fraction in at least one of (8)--(9).
This proves (15).

For the example, exact clipping of (16) by
\[
S=0,\qquad T=0,\qquad S+T=-1
\]
gives (17).  Direct substitution of \(P^\ast\) into (5), in the cyclic
edge order displayed in (16), gives
\[
\left(
-\frac{641}{100},
\frac{17}{100},
-\frac{41}{25},
-\frac{1781}{100},
-\frac{2053}{50},
-\frac{73}{2}
\right).
\tag{30}
\]
Thus only (19) is visible.  Its endpoints and \(P^\ast\) have both
coordinates strictly positive, so its fan triangle lies in
\(\mathcal Q\).  Equations (28)--(29) give (21), and the deepest-point
claim follows from the preceding convex-combination argument.  This
also proves the failure of effective-spanning-chord domination.

Finally, (23) and \(k=b+\Delta\) give
\[
u_i+v_i+d_i+e_i
=h_0+\frac{2\Delta}{9},
\]
which is (25).  Summing it gives
\[
\sum_i e_i=\frac{2\Delta}{3}-G.
\]
If \(S_{\rm add}\) is the total added singleton area, then
\[
\Delta=S_{\rm add}+D_{\rm add},\qquad
\sum_i e_i=S_{\rm add}+2D_{\rm add}.
\]
Eliminating \(S_{\rm add}\) proves (26).  Writing the three added
doubleton areas as \(z_{12},z_{13},z_{23}\), one has
\[
e_1=z_1+z_{12}+z_{13},\qquad
D_{\rm add}=z_{12}+z_{13}+z_{23}.
\]
Therefore \(z_1\geq e_1-D_{\rm add}\), and (25)--(26) give (27).

The four degeneracy statements follow directly from (5)--(6).  In
particular, parallelism to a wall changes only which endpoint
coordinates coincide; the determinant reach and the clipping fraction
remain finite.  A wall coordinate equal to zero is already one of the
continuous boundary cases in (6), and a zero determinant reach
multiplies the corresponding summand by zero.
statement:
Let \(f_1,f_2,f_3\) be nonconstant affine functions on
\(\mathbb R^2\), with pairwise nonparallel linear parts and
\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1.
\]
Let \(B\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a compact two-dimensional convex polygon
containing
\[
\mathcal T=\{f_1,f_2,f_3\leq0\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Use the affine coordinates
\[
S=f_2,\qquad T=f_3,
\tag{2}
\]
and put
\[
\gamma=\frac1{|\det(\nabla f_2,\nabla f_3)|}.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus physical area is \(\gamma\) times coordinate area, and the open
singleton-\(1\) chamber is
\[
\mathcal Q=\{S>0,\ T>0\}.
\tag{4}
\]

Write the counterclockwise vertices of \(B\) cyclically as
\[
V_j=(S_j,T_j),\qquad j\in\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z,
\]
and put
\[
D_j=V_{j+1}-V_j.
\]
For \(X=(S_X,T_X)\), define the signed exterior support violation
\[
\lambda_j(X)
=-\det(D_j,X-V_j).
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(B\) is counterclockwise,
\[
\lambda_j(X)\leq0\qquad(X\in B).
\]
An edge \(j\) is visible from \(X\) exactly when
\(\lambda_j(X)>0\).

For three real numbers \(a,b,c\), let
\[
a_{(1)}\leq a_{(2)}\leq a_{(3)}
\]
be their increasing rearrangement and define
\[
\vartheta(a,b,c)=
\begin{cases}
0,&a_{(1)}\geq0,\\[2mm]
1,&a_{(3)}\leq0\text{ and }a_{(1)}<0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{a_{(1)}^2}
{(a_{(2)}-a_{(1)})(a_{(3)}-a_{(1)})},
&a_{(1)}<0\leq a_{(2)},\\[4mm]
\displaystyle
1-\frac{a_{(3)}^2}
{(a_{(3)}-a_{(1)})(a_{(3)}-a_{(2)})},
&a_{(2)}<0<a_{(3)}.
\end{cases}
\tag{6}
\]
If all three numbers vanish, set \(\vartheta=0\).  This is the area
fraction of a nondegenerate triangle on which an affine function whose
vertex values are \(a,b,c\) is nonpositive.

Let \(K\supseteq B\) be any compact convex body and choose
\[
P=(S_P,T_P)\in K\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}.
\]
Then the added transverse cap areas
\[
e_2=|(K\setminus B)\cap\{S\leq0\}|,\qquad
e_3=|(K\setminus B)\cap\{T\leq0\}|
\tag{7}
\]
satisfy the sharp visible-chain bounds
\[
\boxed{\quad
e_2\geq
\frac{\gamma}{2}
\sum_{j:\lambda_j(P)>0}
\lambda_j(P)\,
\vartheta(S_j,S_{j+1},S_P),
\quad}
\tag{8}
\]
\[
\boxed{\quad
e_3\geq
\frac{\gamma}{2}
\sum_{j:\lambda_j(P)>0}
\lambda_j(P)\,
\vartheta(T_j,T_{j+1},T_P).
\quad}
\tag{9}
\]
The visible indices form one cyclic interval.  The bounds are
simultaneously equalities for
\[
K=\operatorname{conv}(B\cup\{P\}).
\tag{10}
\]

Equivalently, if the supporting line of edge \(j\) is written
\[
a_jS+b_jT=c_j,\qquad
B\subseteq\{a_jS+b_jT\leq c_j\},
\]
then
\[
\lambda_j(P)
=
\frac{|D_j|}{\sqrt{a_j^2+b_j^2}}
\left(a_jS_P+b_jT_P-c_j\right).
\tag{11}
\]
Thus (8)--(9) depend only on the chain vertices, support slopes, and
the support reaches of \(P\).

One may make the word deepest precise without changing the conclusion.
Define the polygonal support depth
\[
\delta_B(X)=\max_j\bigl(\lambda_j(X)\bigr)_+.
\tag{12}
\]
Compactness gives a maximizer \(P\) of \(\delta_B\) on
\(K\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}\), and (8)--(9) apply to that \(P\).
If \(K=\operatorname{conv}(B\cup\{P\})\), this chosen point is deepest
whenever \(\delta_B(P)>0\).

The exact zero-charge configuration is also determined by the chain.
Call an edge charging if at least one endpoint is strictly outside the
closed singleton quadrant:
\[
\mathcal J_{\rm ch}
=
\{j:\min(S_j,S_{j+1})<0
\text{ or }\min(T_j,T_{j+1})<0\}.
\tag{13}
\]
Define the zero-charge visibility region
\[
\mathcal Z_B
=
\overline{\mathcal Q}\cap
\bigcap_{j\in\mathcal J_{\rm ch}}
\{X:\lambda_j(X)\leq0\}.
\tag{14}
\]
For \(P\) in the open quadrant,
\[
\boxed{\quad
\text{the right sides of both (8) and (9) vanish}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
P\in\mathcal Z_B.
\quad}
\tag{15}
\]
Hence a multi-edge frontier can carry positive added singleton area
with no transverse triangle charge whenever
\(\mathcal Z_B\setminus B\) has positive area.

There is no universal effective-spanning-chord domination.  In the
\((S,T)\)-plane let
\[
B^\ast=\operatorname{conv}\left\{
(2,-5),\left(4,\frac12\right),
\left(\frac52,3\right),\left(\frac12,4\right),
(-5,2),(-3,-3)
\right\}.
\tag{16}
\]
It contains the central triangle, and its seven exact cell areas are
\[
\begin{aligned}
b_1&=\frac{1015}{88},&
b_2&=\frac{86}{15},&
b_3&=\frac{86}{15},\\
b_{12}&=\frac{1322}{165},&
b_{13}&=\frac{1322}{165},&
b_{23}&=\frac{121}{10},&
b_{123}&=\frac12.
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
Take
\[
P^\ast=\left(\frac{33}{10},\frac{89}{50}\right),
\qquad
K^\ast=\operatorname{conv}(B^\ast\cup\{P^\ast\}).
\tag{18}
\]
Only the edge
\[
\left[\left(4,\frac12\right),\left(\frac52,3\right)\right]
\tag{19}
\]
is visible from \(P^\ast\), with
\[
\lambda(P^\ast)=\frac{17}{100}.
\tag{20}
\]
All three vertices of its fan triangle lie in the open singleton
quadrant.  Therefore
\[
|(K^\ast\setminus B^\ast)\cap\mathcal Q|
=\frac{17}{200}>0,
\qquad e_2=e_3=0.
\tag{21}
\]
The point \(P^\ast\) is deepest in the sense of (12).  Thus neither an
individual chain face nor a pair of adjacent faces is guaranteed to
give the positive lower bound supplied by a transverse spanning chord.

For connection with the crossing ledger, now additionally let
\(A_0,A_2\) be compact two-dimensional convex bodies, let
\[
B=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2},\qquad
M=|A_0|,\qquad m=|A_2|,
\]
and let \(L_1,L_2,L_3\) be endpoint offsets.  Define
\[
u_i=|A_0\cap\{f_i\leq L_i\}|,\qquad
v_i=|A_2\cap\{f_i\leq-L_i\}|.
\tag{22}
\]
For a compact convex \(K\supseteq B\), put
\[
k=|K|,\qquad
c_i=|K\cap\{f_i\leq0\}|,
\]
and assume all three crossing equalities
\[
u_i+v_i+c_i=\frac{2(M+m+k)}9
\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\tag{23}
\]
Write
\[
b=|B|,\qquad
d_i=|B\cap\{f_i\leq0\}|,\qquad
\Delta=k-b,
\]
\[
e_i=|(K\setminus B)\cap\{f_i\leq0\}|
\qquad(i=1,2,3),
\]
\[
h_0=\frac{2(M+m+b)}9,\qquad
\rho_i=u_i+v_i+d_i-h_0,\qquad
G=\rho_1+\rho_2+\rho_3.
\tag{24}
\]
Then
\[
e_i=c_i-d_i=\frac{2\Delta}{9}-\rho_i.
\tag{25}
\]
Because (1) makes the added triple cell null, the total added
doubleton area is
\[
D_{\rm add}=-\frac{\Delta}{3}-G.
\tag{26}
\]
If \(z_1\) is the total added singleton-\(1\) area, then
\[
z_1\geq e_1-D_{\rm add}
=\frac{5\Delta}{9}+\rho_2+\rho_3.
\tag{27}
\]
Equations (8)--(9) are therefore the exact local triangle charges
available once an added extreme point leaves \(\mathcal Z_B\).  Formula
(27) alone does not force this: the exact example (16)--(21) exhibits
a positive-capacity region where the right sides of (8)--(9) are both
zero.  A complete residual proof needs a quantitative upper bound on
the total singleton area that a convex extension can add while all its
new singleton extreme points remain in \(\mathcal Z_B\).

The formulas include all requested degeneracies:

- If an edge is parallel to \(S=0\) or \(T=0\), (5), (8), and (9)
  remain unchanged; no division by its slope occurs.
- If an endpoint or \(P\) lies on a wall, its corresponding entry in
  (6) is zero and the displayed continuous clipping fraction gives the
  exact area.
- If \(\lambda_j(P)=0\), that face has zero reach and contributes zero.
- If an edge has zero length, then \(D_j=0\) and
  \(\lambda_j(P)=0\); deleting the repeated vertex leaves every sum
  unchanged.
